title: Pre-menopausal women, classified as hypo- or hyperresponders, do not alter their LDL/HDL ratio following a high dietary cholesterol challenge
authors: Herron KL, Vega-Lopez S, Conde K, Ramjiganesh T, Roy S, Shachter NS, et al.
journal: Journal of the American College of Nutrition
followUp: Two 30-day periods separated by a 3-week washout
population: Normolipidaemic premenopausal women aged 18 to 49 years, 29 Caucasian and 22 of Hispanic origin
funder: Funded by the American Egg Board.
result: Randomised crossover trial of eggs supplying 640 mg additional dietary cholesterol per day against placebo (0 mg additional cholesterol per day). LDL and HDL cholesterol rose in Hispanic and Caucasian women without a change in the LDL/HDL ratio. Hyporesponders, defined by a rise in total cholesterol of less than 0.05 mmol/L per additional 100 mg dietary cholesterol per day, showed no rise in LDL or HDL cholesterol; both rose in hyperresponders (0.06 mmol/L or more per 100 mg), who also had higher apo C-III, apo B and CETP. The authors concluded that excess dietary cholesterol does not increase the risk of developing an atherogenic lipoprotein profile in premenopausal women, regardless of response classification. Values read from the abstract and the publisher's article page; the full text was not accessible.
